column1: # *** THE FIRST QUERIES AIMED AT SPAIN, 15 September 2026. ***
# Felix Llerena and Rosalia Aguilar, named as naturales de Cordova on the marriage act of 8 January 1791.
# *** The control was run BEFORE the null was believed. That is the whole point of this file. ***
*** THE PARENT-PAIR QUERY, RUN ON FELIX LLERENA AND ROSALIA AGUILAR ***
column2: *** 'Llerena y de Rosalia Aguilar' returns ZERO. *** The page rendered and reported a count of 0 - it was not a blocked page. *** 'Felix Llerena' *** returns results, but every one is modern Latin America - Cartagena, Peru, Mexico - where the name is common. *** 'Rosalia Aguilar' *** returns forty collections, of which *** only two are in Spain at all ***: La Carolina, Jaen, notarial records of 1829-1837 - wrong province and forty years too late.
column4: *** AND ON ITS OWN THAT WOULD MEAN NOTHING, WHICH IS WHY THE CONTROL WAS RUN FIRST THIS TIME. ***

column1: *** THE CONTROL - RUN BEFORE THE NULL WAS BELIEVED, NOT AFTER ***
column2: *** Searching 'ciudad de Cordova' and reading the COLLECTION names that come back. *** The Andalusian collections in FamilySearch full text are *** Nobility Records - Granada 1489-1718, Ecija 1529-1907 *** - plus *** Madrid notarial protocols *** and *** Orders of Chivalry induction files ***. *** The only 'Cordoba' that appears is Cordoba, VERACRUZ, in Mexico. ***
column4: *** SO THE FULL-TEXT INDEX FOR ANDALUSIA HOLDS NOBILITY AND NOTARIAL RECORDS, NOT PARISH REGISTERS. *** An eighteenth-century Cordoba baptism or marriage is *** not in the corpus being searched ***. *** THEREFORE THE ZERO ABOVE IS 'NOT FINDABLE BY THIS INSTRUMENT', NOT 'NOT THERE' ***, and it is recorded that way. *** This is the Berroeta lesson applied forwards instead of backwards *** - there the control came after a day of work had been planned on an unchecked assumption; here it came before a single conclusion was drawn.

column1: *** ONE THING THE NULL DOES SUPPORT, WEAKLY ***
column2: *** Within the corpus that IS indexed - Spanish nobility and hidalguia files, chivalric orders, Madrid protocols - the pair returns nothing. ***
column4: *** THAT IS WEAK EVIDENCE THAT FELIX LLERENA AND ROSALIA AGUILAR WERE NOT ARMIGEROUS GENTRY WITH A CHANCILLERIA FILE. *** Those are precisely the records that are indexed, and they are searchable back to 1489. *** It bears on this archive's long argument about 'de Llerena' as a toponymic ***, and it sits with the 1811 act calling Sancho *** 'Don' *** while the 1798 deposition records that *** he could not write his own name. *** *** Weak evidence is still evidence, and it points away from hidalguia. ***

column1: *** WHAT HAS TO HAPPEN BEFORE CORDOBA CAN BE SEARCHED AT ALL ***
column2: *** Establish whether Cordoba city parish registers of about 1740-1790 are FILMED, and whether any are indexed. *** Neither is known. The way in is an image's own Information panel, *** NOT a catalogue line, which has failed twice in this archive today. ***
column4: *** THIS IS NOW THE GATING ITEM FOR THE WHOLE SPANISH PROGRAMME. *** Four people wait behind it: *** Sancho's baptism about 1767, the marriage of Felix and Rosalia, and the Asturian parish of Rodrigo and Rosa Fernandez. *** Until the corpus is mapped, *** every Spanish null this archive produces is uninterpretable. ***

column1: *** THE GRANADA INDEX, SEARCHED FOR FELIX AND ROSALIA - AND TWO NULLS THROWN AWAY FIRST ***
column2: *** Exact-surname searches returned zero twice *** - 'Llerena' + spouse 'Aguilar', and 'Lerena' + spouse 'Aguilar', Spain 1720-1800, both with the 'No Results Found' line present. *** BOTH WERE DISCARDED. *** The control: the same exact-match shape, run for 1750-1760, *** fails to retrieve the 1754 act that is KNOWN to be in that collection *** - because the indexed surname is the compound *** 'Lerena y Armenta' ***, which exact matching will not reach.
column3: *** DISCARDED - the query could not find a record known to exist ***
column4: *** A NULL FROM A QUERY THAT CANNOT FIND WHAT IS THERE IS NOT A NULL. *** Recorded because the temptation was to report two clean zeros and move on.

column1: *** THE WORKING SHAPE, AND THE CONTROL THAT PASSED ***
column2: *** Non-exact surname, exact given names, place Spain, dates 1735-1785. *** Run for the known couple - Sancho + Ana Maria - it returns *** 263 results including the Granada Catholic Pre-Marriage Investigation Files and the full 1754 marriage record ***. *** So the shape works and that collection is reachable by it. ***
column4: *** ONLY NOW IS A NULL WORTH ANYTHING. ***

column1: *** AND IT IS A NULL: FELIX LLERENA AND ROSALIA AGUILAR ARE NOT IN THE ANDALUSIAN INDEXES ***
column2: *** The same shape, for Felix + Rosalia, Spain 1735-1785, returns 305 results and NOT ONE ANDALUSIAN COLLECTION among them. *** What comes back is Spain Catholic Church Records, Spain Baptisms, Gerona Municipal Records and the Diocese of Santander - *** nothing from Granada, Cordoba, Sevilla, Jaen or Malaga. ***
column4: *** THEIR MARRIAGE IS NOT INDEXED BY FAMILYSEARCH, ANYWHERE IN ANDALUSIA, IN THE FIFTY YEARS THAT MUST CONTAIN IT. *** Their son was born about 1767. *** Taken with the mapping - that Cordoba's parish registers are not on FamilySearch at all - this closes the searchable routes. *** *** What is left is the Archivo General del Obispado de Cordoba, which is a letter and is already logged as David's. *** *** It also means the 1791 act remains the ONLY document in the world this archive has that names Felix Llerena and Rosalia Aguilar. ***
